title: Chest pain
personality: Worried, a little short of breath when talking, answers briefly and to the point
chief_complaint: Doctor, I have this pressing pain in my chest, and it keeps coming back.
history_present_illness: For about a year I sometimes had chest pressure when climbing stairs, it went away after 2-3 minutes of rest. Over the last 5 days the pain comes more often, after walking only one block, and lasts up to 15 minutes. Yesterday evening it came even at rest while watching TV and lasted about 15 minutes. A neighbour gave me a nitroglycerin tablet under the tongue and the pain eased after a few minutes. Today in the morning it happened again at rest.

symptoms.name: chest pain
symptoms.details: behind the breastbone, pressing, squeezing, like a heavy weight; 7 out of 10; lasts 10-15 minutes; started a year ago only on stairs, the last 5 days much more often and now even at rest

symptoms.name: pain spreading
symptoms.details: goes to the left arm and sometimes to the left side of the jaw

symptoms.name: relief
symptoms.details: rest helped before; nitroglycerin under the tongue helped yesterday within a few minutes

negative_symptoms: pain when pressing on the chest
pain that changes with body position
past_medical_history: High blood pressure for 10 years, takes pills irregularly. Told about 'high cholesterol' two years ago but did not treat it. No diabetes known. No operations.
medications: Enalapril 10 mg, often forgets to take it. Took one nitroglycerin tablet yesterday.
family_history: Father had a heart attack at 58 and died at 62. Mother has diabetes.
social_history: Smokes about one pack a day for 35 years. Alcohol on weekends, 2-3 beers. Sits at the wheel 10-12 hours a day, little physical activity. Married, two adult children.

test_results.General inspection: Overweight (BMI 31). Anxious. Skin of normal colour, no cyanosis. No peripheral oedema.
test_results.Heart auscultation: Rhythm regular. Heart sounds slightly muffled, accent of the 2nd sound over the aorta. No murmurs, no pericardial rub.
test_results.Lung auscultation: Vesicular breathing over all fields, no crackles or wheezes.
test_results.ECG: Sinus rhythm 88/min. Horizontal ST-segment depression of 1 mm in V4-V6 and T-wave inversion in I, aVL recorded during pain; resolves after the pain episode. No ST elevation, no pathological Q waves.
test_results.Troponin I: High-sensitivity troponin I: 6 ng/L at admission and 7 ng/L after 3 hours (reference < 26 ng/L) — not elevated, no dynamic rise.
test_results.Lipid profile: Total cholesterol 6.8 mmol/L, LDL 4.6 mmol/L, HDL 0.9 mmol/L, triglycerides 2.3 mmol/L.
test_results.Chest X-ray: No infiltrates. Cardiac silhouette within normal limits. Aorta not widened.
test_results.Echocardiography: LV ejection fraction 55%. Mild hypokinesia of the lateral wall. Mild LV hypertrophy. Valves intact, no pericardial effusion.
